analysis: Examined the EngineV2Bridge.swift head/base text and the new AdmissionRateEstimators.swift patch. Changes to the bridge are limited to new state (observedDecodeShapeEwma, admissionFixes, calibratedIsolatedPrefillTps), a new init parameter admissionFixes, and one init assignment (performanceMeasurements.keepsNewestObservationTime). The prefix-cache construction, SSD store and hybrid checkpoint acceptance, staging backstops, request-ID handling and shutdown logic are unchanged, so T-041, A-001 and A-004 posture is unaffected. The new file adds a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES env toggle (default on; a local operator can disable it, which only reverts to the previous estimators). It also adds pure functions: decodeRateShape selects per-batch or per-row decode charging, and IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate.resolve anchors and expires the isolated prefill rate. These handle only numeric performance estimates with isfinite and positivity guards. They touch no plaintext, keys, attestation or authorization, and no trust boundary. Availability or routing impact is limited to the provider's own deadline admission, which a malicious local operator already controls (ADV-001 can alter the provider itself). The operator could manipulate the rate evidence, but that is no new capability: the operator already controls the provider process, and the coordinator remains the policy authority. Not examined: callers that consume these helpers (the Admission, Accounting and calibration files, and the EnginePerformanceMeasurements.keepsNewestObservationTime and CBv2DecodeRateShape definitions). They are outside the supplied evidence. I found no security regression in the supplied evidence, but a downstream pass could check whether the stale-evidence expiry (30 min) or anchor floor lets a request be admitted that would previously be refused, as a DoS or availability concern. That concern is low and speculative.
